          Added — Diagnostic Battery per ADOM; Diagnose Log Collection in every device ADOM (2026-10-14)

          • Security: the console accepted any diagnose command. The read-only gate (ssh_ops.assert_readonly) allowed every line starting with diagnose or diag, so the appliance SSH Console and the Log Collection custom-commands box would send diagnose debug kernel sysrq command crash, diagnose ha failover … or diagnose sys kill …. Every diagnose statement is now checked by name and refused when a word changes the device: kill, clear, reset, delete, failover, sysrq/crash, enable/disable, set, format, fsck, rmmod and similar. Abbreviations count, because the CLI completes them: diag sys kil 11 1 reads as kill. get and show are unchanged.
          • New page: Administrator → Diagnostic Battery (user_manage), in each device ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator). An administrator chooses the commands that make up the ADOM's battery. Commands can be ticked from a tree discovered on a real device of the ADOM or typed by hand. Save keeps the order of the commands already in the battery, and Reset to default returns to the product default. The Global ADOM shows a read-only summary of the five batteries.
          • Discovery reads the device's own diagnose tree. It types <path> ? on the device CLI over SSH, walks the tree and stores the result per product and firmware build. Each node is classified by its name and by the device's description of it before it is asked, and a refused node is never asked. Measured in the lab: FortiGate 8.0.1, 3,015 nodes in about ten minutes; FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7, 612; FortiADC 8.0.4, 598. FortiWeb and FortiADC close the SSH session when ? follows a node with exactly one child (diagnose hardware cpu), so such a node is read by TAB completion on a new session. When FortiAuthenticator does not answer a ?, the node is asked again. On FortiWeb, ? after some leaves runs the (read-only) command, so the page recommends running discovery on a lab unit or in a maintenance window.
          • The battery rule. A battery refuses state-changing commands by name, by the device's description of the command or of any parent ("Kill a process.", "set/get debug level…", "Generate one system info log file every 2 minutes."), and, because a battery runs unattended, commands that never return, flood the session or send traffic (top, sniffer, debug flow, ping, traceroute, test). The rule is checked when the battery is saved and again before each run.
          • Diagnose Log Collection moves to Operations › Troubleshooting in all five device ADOMs; until now it was a FortiWeb-only entry under Operations. It runs the active ADOM's battery, which is listed read-only on the page, with a link to the editor for administrators. If a device's build does not have a command (according to that build's discovery), the command is skipped and the report says SKIPPED: not present in <build>. Output such as "Command fail" or "Parsing error" is tagged [not available on this build]. The custom box follows the battery rule. The FortiWeb default battery has 28 commands: diagnose debug proxy log 3 is gone. It printed nothing on 7.6.8 or 8.0.6, and its parent is described as set/get, meaning the trailing number sets a debug level. The other four products start from small measured defaults.
          • Appliances: "SSH user, if different from the API user". A FortiGate registered with a REST api-user cannot open SSH with that user. Log collection now logs in with the separate SSH user and the separate SSH password. Before this it sent the API password, which failed on FortiAuthenticator, whose REST key SSH refuses.
          • Processes: the "Collect diagnostic logs" step runs the device's own battery. It ran FortiWeb's battery on every product. It now runs the battery of the device's ADOM, planned against its build exactly like Diagnose Log Collection, and its result says how many commands ran and how many were skipped.
          • Fixed: the one-at-a-time guards of log collection and rediscovery read their start time in local time. The stamp is UTC, so on a node whose clock is not UTC a running collection looked hours older (UTC+N) or younger (UTC−N) than it was, and a second run could start beside it. Nodes on UTC, such as the reference pair, were not affected.
          • Migration diagbat01: tables diag_catalogs and diag_batteries, and the column appliances.ssh_username.

          Security — the operator CLI no longer runs the app tree as root (2026-10-14)

          • satom under sudo drops to the service account before executing anything from /opt/satom. Diagnostics ran git status as root inside the repository, which executes what the service account's .git/config names (core.fsmonitor, measured); every venv snippet (_app_call: update/promote enqueue, backups, scheduler and device actions, the automatic backup db of execute update package), flask one-shots, diagnose python and the support bundle ran the venv python or pip as root; execute reinstall venv ran pip install -r requirements.txt as root and then chowned the result recursively, following symlinks. All of these now run as the service account (runuser -m -u, or setpriv to the tree's uid when it has no name); the venv is built as that account and nothing is chowned afterwards. A test fails on any git/venv/flask/pip command the CLI builds without the drop.
          • Root no longer writes or chowns through the service account's directories. execute repair permissions chowned whatever a symlink in data/ pointed to (e.g. /etc/shadow) to the service account; it now walks by directory fd, never follows a link and skips hard-linked files. Update packages and API packs are staged in data/ by a child that already dropped privileges (execute update fetch downloads into a root-private directory first), queue files are created exclusively and without following links, and every remaining chown is follow_symlinks=False.

          Security — signed releases, node request signing, console hardening (2026-10-14)

          • Signed-release enforcement is activatable without blocking HA. With a root-owned trust anchor (/etc/satom/release-trust.allowed_signers, or a single key at …/release-trust.pub), root-side content — unit files, the install-*.sh scripts, the operator CLI and the runner copies — comes from the newest signed release: the target itself, or its signed ancestor when deploy/ is identical. An unsigned change to deploy/ no longer refuses the update: the application updates and only the root-side refresh is held, shown as a warning, so the standby keeps converging. New satom execute sign-release (dry run by default; signs on the primary with a root-only key and pushes) and satom get release trust; the satom execute reinstall verbs are gated the same way. Root now verifies inside a root-only mirror and never runs git inside the service account's repository (the first version ran that repository's configured programs as root), and the .pub single-key anchor now works. With no anchor, behaviour is unchanged.
          • Node-to-node requests are HMAC-signed. Every peer request carries X-SATOM-Node-Ts + X-SATOM-Node-Sig (HMAC-SHA256 over method, path+query, timestamp and body hash, keyed with the node identity key). The raw key never crosses the wire, signatures older than 120 s are refused, and the static X-FM-Node-Key header is no longer accepted. The peer certificate must now verify (system trust store or internal CA): an untrusted certificate is refused with a logged reason instead of silently downgrading. Emergency override: SATOM_PEER_TLS_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1. Both nodes must run this release; expect about a minute of "not authenticated" peer views while the standby catches up, and keep both clocks NTP-synchronised.
          • The database console runs under a dedicated read-only role. The console, report widgets and plugin datasets now run every query as satom_console_ro: no monitoring privileges, no access to the credential tables or credential columns (list columns explicitly instead of SELECT * on appliances or managed certificates), and refused outright when the role is not provisioned — never a fallback to the application role. Provisioned by the installer and on update by deploy/install-console-role.sh (primary only; the standby gets it by replication).
          • The metrics store's admin endpoints require keys (delete, snapshot, force-merge, reload, flags, pprof…), generated into a root-only /etc/satom/metrics-auth.env by install-metrics-store.sh; the application only holds the snapshot key it needs.
          • The Device Console gate reads Fortinet abbreviations the way the CLI does. Any prefix — exe fa, exe reb, set passw, quoted keywords, ? help keys — is classified as forbidden or needs acknowledgement (before, exe fa sent a factory reset as an ordinary line). Transcripts and TAC bundles redact abbreviated and compound secret attributes.
          • Scout checks a typed Published host by host and port against the appliance inventory, not by host alone.

          Fixed — monitoring and source of truth (2026-10-14)

          • FortiAnalyzer CPU and memory probes read the 7.6 get system performance block layout: {device} graded "error" on every sample and stayed "degraded". Memory is physical RAM, like FortiWeb/FortiADC.
          • The FortiADC/FortiAnalyzer box-metrics scrape writes its CPU and memory series: it read keys the parser never produced, so both were always empty.
          • The source-of-truth identity drops FortiAnalyzer's per-read salted ["ENC", …] secrets as a backstop to the sweep scrub, so an unchanged box can never again mint an hourly version and drift alert. The "ENC …" strings FortiWeb/FortiADC store are still compared.
          • Config-drift alerting no longer mutes a device named {device} by default; alerts.drift_exclude is empty unless the operator sets it.
          • The HA datasync no longer copies the integration-hook queue (data/integrations/queue/, claimed/) to the standby. The hook runner is meant to be enabled on both nodes; with the queue replicated, the standby would have run every pending hook a second time, which is why it had been left disabled there (and hooks would not have run after a failover).

          Changed — FortiADC API library (2026-10-14)

          • REST↔CLI field renames measured value by value on {device} (7.6.7, 115) and {device} (8.0.4, 85) are now one field under the REST name (e.g. pool = load-balance-pool), so they no longer read "unverified on this build"; 7.6.7 goes from 967 to 1,082 fields "both". A build that was not measured gets no renames.
          • The schema harvest runs a read-only REST shape probe on FortiADC: top-level objects and child tables by ?pkey=. A 404 at a child path is not recorded as absent, because FortiADC serves some children only inside the parent row.

          Changed — navigation labels (2026-10-14)

          • Log Collection is now Diagnose Log Collection (menu, page title, translations). Its battery lost two commands that never returned data on FortiWeb 7.6.8 or 8.0.6: diagnose hardware harddisk on its own (it only prints "you must specify cmd"; its list, info, health, errors and attributes sub-commands stay) and diagnose system ha export-eventlog (it needs parameters). diagnose hardware cpu printed nothing on both builds and is now diagnose hardware cpu list, which answers. The firmware-flash before/after battery reuses the same list.
          • The Fleet group is gone; Operations is the first group of every device ADOM. It opens with the fleet pages and then holds Device Backups, Log Collection and Import Backup (and Template Library for profiles outside Administrator). The device's own menu now follows Operations. The Global ADOM keeps its Global block and has no Operations group.
          • The API console is a sub-menu of Automation (Automation › API › Registry & console) instead of a group of its own. A profile that may open the console (registry.view) but cannot see Automation (no config_write) keeps the standalone API group, so no profile loses the page and none sees it twice. Every entry keeps its own permission: the menu moved, access did not change.
          • Troubleshooting (under Operations in the device ADOMs, in the Global block in Global) holds Backend Reachability, Config Compare, Path Diagnostics and Scout; the separate Troubleshooting entries under Operations and the flat entries in the Global list are gone. The fleet pages run Dashboard (where an ADOM has one), Calendar, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring, Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting, then Fleet Objects and WAF (FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs only) and Jobs last.
          • The fault-localisation ladder formerly called "Scout" is labelled Path Diagnostics; the AI assistant formerly called "AI Advisor" is labelled Scout; the firmware release-notes reviewer formerly shown as "Scout" is the Upgrade Advisory, and when it is unavailable it says Path Diagnostics must be switched on in Settings → Path Diagnostics — the switch it actually uses. Menu, page titles, settings panes and messages; URLs and bookmarks are unchanged.
          • In the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs, Operations › Troubleshooting holds Scout only: Backend Reachability, Config Compare and Path Diagnostics work on FortiWeb and FortiADC objects and are no longer listed there. The pages still open by URL.

          Changed — ADOM Search searches each ADOM's own configuration (2026-10-14)

          • The Search page is titled ADOM Search (it was "Global Search") and searches the configuration SATOM last synced from the appliances of the active ADOM — FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator or FortiAnalyzer, or all of them in the Global ADOM. It used to query five FortiWeb REST paths live and send them to every device that was not a FortiADC, so a FortiAuthenticator RADIUS client, a FortiGate address or a FortiAnalyzer managed device was never found.
          • Every synced collection is searched, not a fixed list. Each match shows the section, type, object (with its parent object for sub-table rows), field and value, and each appliance shows when its configuration was last synced. An appliance with no synced configuration is named as not searched.
          • The Object Type filter is replaced by Section, listing the sections the ADOM's appliances actually have. The subtitle, placeholder and tips are specific to each ADOM.
          • Passwords, keys, pre-shared secrets and ENC values are never matched or shown, so the search cannot be used to guess a secret.
          • The top-bar search button is also shown in the FortiAnalyzer ADOM. Menu entry, URL and bookmarks are unchanged.

          Security — infrastructure hardening (2026-10-13 internal code audit)

          • Node-to-node transport is HTTPS-only and certificate-verified. The peer probes between the two HA nodes no longer fall back to plain HTTP, so the shared identity key can never cross the wire in cleartext, and the peer's TLS certificate is now validated against the system trust store (the public fleet wildcard) or the internal CA. A genuinely untrusted certificate still connects, but over encrypted TLS and with a logged warning, so the health dashboards never break.
          • HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) is now sent on every response, scoped to the node's own host (no includeSubDomains/preload, so sibling fleet services are unaffected).
          • The integration-hook sandbox can no longer read the secret files. The unprivileged hook runner masks /opt/satom/.env, the internal-CA key under pki/ and the HA key under .ssh/, and hides other processes, so a hook cannot reach the Fernet key or database URL on disk.

          Security — second round of the 2026-10-13 internal code audit

          Accounts and sign-in - A password-reset link is now single-use: it is tied to the current password and stops working the moment the password changes. - A TOTP code can no longer be used twice inside its time window. - The sign-in page no longer reveals that an account is disabled or awaiting approval before the password is checked, and an unknown username now takes the same time as a real one. - Setting a recovery email, starting 2FA setup, enabling 2FA and regenerating backup codes now require the current password (and, when 2FA is already on, a current code), the same proof disabling 2FA already asked for. Enabling 2FA refuses to overwrite an authenticator that is already set up. The Settings → Security forms carry the extra fields.

          Directory sign-in - An account imported from one directory can only be signed into through that same directory. A directory that merely shares the account name can no longer take it over, and login never rewrites an existing account's source. - The Active Directory membership check escapes the name and prefers the exact signed-in identity, so a like-named account in another domain cannot pass.

          Authorization - The read-write Device Console now requires the device-apply permission, not any minor edit permission. - Turning off an appliance's TLS verification now requires the password again, like changing its host. - A template cannot be approved by its own author. - CLI-coverage evidence and dumps from a device in maintenance mode are hidden from users who may not see that device. - A non-admin can no longer schedule or run an automation against a device hidden from them, and their "all targets" no longer reaches hidden devices.

          Stored markup - Values that come from a managed appliance or from another user (device and host names, log lines, policy and signature names, error text) are escaped before being placed in the page, on the Logs, Settings, Exceptions, Object editor, Server-Policy wizard, FortiAnalyzer and analysis views.

          Security — fixes from the 2026-10-13 internal code audit

          Appliance command injection - Certificate import (and the certificate carry between appliances) accepted a backslash inside a PEM or passphrase. The device CLI treats \ as an escape inside a quoted value, so a key ending in \ kept the quote open and the lines after it ran as raw configuration commands, for example creating an administrator. PEM values are now rebuilt from their BEGIN/base64/END lines only, and ", \ and control characters are refused in PEMs and passphrases. A hostile source appliance can no longer inject into the destination during a carry. - The read-only console gates (console, CLI coverage live read, probe and schema gates) passed control characters to the interactive shell, where backspace or Ctrl-U erase the show and leave a write. Every gate now refuses control characters. The write console also classifies abbreviated verbs (exe factoryres, exec reboot) the way the full words are classified.

          Authorization - Changing an appliance's host, port, username or platform kept its stored password, so the next sync sent the device credentials to the new endpoint. The edit form and PUT /api/appliances/<id> now require the password to be entered again for such a change, and the SSH password too when the row holds a separate one. - A user with users.manage or profiles.manage could grant themselves any permission: assign themselves (or create) a wider profile, add keys to the profile they are assigned to, or reset the password or 2FA of a more privileged account. Each of these is now refused unless the actor already holds every permission involved. - An API token owned by a non-admin could run System Automations and actions with no capability mapping (system backup, git bundle, certificate issuing…). These now need an owner with user management, as in the browser.

          Server-side requests - Network Architecture probes, monitor HTTPS probes and process http_check steps could reach the node's own loopback services, including the metrics store, which has no authentication, and cloud metadata addresses. They now go through the target guard, resolve the name once and connect to that address. The node's internal ports (5432, 8000, 8428) are refused in every mode, including the Transaction Tracer, whose inventory mode now checks the port as well as the host. - The DNS tool and process DNS checks refused nothing that starts with -, so an entry such as -f<file> made dig read a local file. Names and servers are now validated.

          Sign-in and sessions - The post-login redirect accepted /<tab>/host, which browsers follow to another site. It now accepts local paths only. - The remember-me cookie is now Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and lasts 14 days (it was not Secure and lasted 365 days). - 2FA: the half-signed-in state expires after 5 minutes, wrong codes count toward the account lockout and are audited (login.2fa_fail), and a correct password no longer resets the failure count before the code is checked. - Any Authorization: Bearer header switched the idle session lock off for a cookie session. Only the API is exempt now.

          Unauthenticated endpoints - /healthz without the inter-node identity key now answers only ok and peer_authenticated. The revision, host statistics and database detail are reserved for the peer node. /healthz/primary no longer returns database error text, and /healthz/backups, /healthz/cert-renewals and /healthz/reconciler answer 403 without the key. An HA pair needs the identity key configured for its peer views (it is, on every pair that shows the encrypted channel as configured).

          Other hardening - The self-update runner (root) validates the request id, the branch and the target, rejects unknown request kinds, and writes status, library and requirements files without following symbolic links. Promote runs the root-owned /usr/local/sbin/satom-promote.sh, never the copy in the application tree; a node without it refuses promote until install-runner.sh is run. Package extraction refuses links already on disk and archives over 2 GiB unpacked. - Regex Lab evaluates each pattern in a separate process killed after 2 seconds, so a catastrophic pattern can no longer hold a web worker. - The read-only SQL console refuses functions that read tables by name inside a string (query_to_xml and the other *_to_xml functions), file and large-object functions, and backend signalling. - Import Backup caps decompressed sizes and no longer writes outside its folder for a device named ..; the flash report no longer creates a folder for any job id it is asked to read.

          Fixed — FortiADC live state was reported as configuration drift

          • A FortiADC returns the live state of some objects inside their configuration rows: a virtual server's or pool's availability (HEALTHY, DEAD …), an interface's availability, and a certificate's status (OK, Expired). Each flip minted a configuration version and raised Config drift … it came from the device side. On the lab box {device} every version since 2026-10-12 — four versions and 20 drift alerts — differed in nothing else, and the device swung back to an earlier version when the virtual server recovered.
          • These fields are no longer part of a configuration version. The rule is keyed by table: status stays configuration in every other FortiADC table, and the configured state next to each stripped field (the virtual server's enable/disable/maintain, the certificate's validity dates) still mints a version when it changes. Existing histories are re-keyed in place on the next sync; it creates no version and no alert.

          Fixed — satom get alerts status said "ok" while every alert email was refused

          • The status judged the settings, not delivery. On a1 the settings were complete and the status said ok while the local mail relay answered 454 4.7.1 Relay access denied to every alert from 2026-09-23 onward: 186 refusals, nothing delivered, alerts reached the in-app bell only.
          • The alert engine now keeps the outcome of its last send attempt, and the status shows it under last email and turns bad when that attempt was not delivered.

          Fixed — alert email: Gmail refused every message without a Message-ID; delivered-but-unsigned is now an error

          • SATOM built its messages without Message-ID and Date. A local Postfix added both on the way out, which hid the gap; any other hand-off is refused by Gmail (550 5.7.1 Messages missing a valid Message-ID header). Every message now carries both headers.
          • Delivered is not received. When the local mail server hands mail straight to the recipient's server with no DKIM signature (Postfix with no relayhost and no signing milter), the message passes SPF at most and Gmail, Outlook and others may file it as spam. SATOM now reports that as a deliverability error: a red box on Settings → Email, a second red line under Send test after a successful send, and in satom get alerts status (last email → deliverability: ERROR, status bad). An external SMTP provider, a relayhost or a signing milter clears it.
          • The Send test result box shows the server's reply as text; it used to insert it as HTML.

          Fixed — two sidebar groups named "Automation", and a Process entry lost next to Studio

          • A profile without user management (operator, read-only) saw the Process page in a group of its own labelled Automation, next to the real Automation group: two groups with one name. That group is now labelled Process.
          • In the Global ADOM a custom profile without user management that holds a Studio permission got the Studio group instead of Process, so a page it may open had no menu entry. It now gets both.
